definitions.explanation: The tiny orange eggs of the flying fish, used as a sushi topping and as a garnish. The grains are much smaller than salmon roe and pop crisply between the teeth.

examples.japanese: とびこの{軍艦|ぐんかん}を{頼|たの}んだ。
examples.english: I ordered a flying-fish-roe gunkan roll.

examples.japanese: とびこはプチプチした{食感|しょっかん}が{楽|たの}しい。
examples.english: Flying fish roe has a fun popping texture.

examples.japanese: {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}のまわりにとびこをまぶすと、{見|み}た{目|め}が{一気|いっき}に{華|はな}やかになる。
examples.english: Coating the outside of a roll with flying fish roe makes it look far more festive at once.

notes:
Written in kana on most menus; the kanji {飛|と}び{子|こ} is rare. Often dyed — green with wasabi, black with squid ink — for color on a platter.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- とびこの{軍艦|ぐんかん}: gunkan sushi topped with flying fish roe
- とびこをのせる: to top something with flying fish roe
- {緑|みどり}のとびこ: wasabi-flavored green roe

SIMILAR WORDS:
- いくら: salmon roe — large, soft, glossy orange spheres
- {数|かず}の{子|こ}: herring roe — a firm block of tiny eggs, eaten at New Year
- {明太子|めんたいこ}: spicy pollock roe — sold as a whole seasoned sac
